finalText:
Rebase and merge both bring one branch's changes into another, but they leave very different history behind.

**Merge** keeps both timelines and adds a new commit that joins them. Nothing is rewritten, so it's always safe, even on shared branches. The trade-off is a messier history with extra "merge commit" clutter.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of the other branch, one by one, so history ends up looking like a straight line. It's cleaner to read later, but it rewrites commit history — which is dangerous on any branch other people are also using, since their copies won't match anymore.

Rule of thumb: rebase your own local, not-yet-shared branch to tidy it up before merging in. Once a branch is shared or public, merge instead of rebasing it.
